sermon.title: The Kingdom of God and Those Outside It
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: From Mark 4:11 Pastor David G. Kincer explains that knowledge of the mystery of the kingdom is given, hidden in parables from those who close their eyes. He lays out the steps into the kingdom, who will not inherit it, who the “dogs” and sleeping watchmen are, what the kingdom is—righteousness, peace and joy in power—and how believers should live wisely before those outside.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: One word in “they could quote the [unclear]” (15:10) was not clear. Caption fixes include “earthen vessels,” “sulfuric acid,” “parable of the sower,” “John 3:3.” He says science shows one shot of whiskey is intoxication (unchecked). Sensitive content kept as spoken: homosexuality and sexual sins listed, Catholic idols, greedy ministers, politicians getting rich, Jews and Romans killing Jesus (with his point that every sinner pierced him).

chunks.section_question: What is “given” to those who know the mystery of the kingdom?
chunks.short_answer: From Mark 4:11 and its parallels (Matthew 13, Acts 28, Isaiah 6) he says knowledge of the mystery of the kingdom of God is given—not acquired or paid for. A mystery is something hidden you must search for, and the kingdom is the dominion ruled by God; those without that knowledge are outside the kingdom.

chunks.section_question: Who are the “dogs” outside the city?
chunks.short_answer: He says “dogs” is a parable, not animals in heaven. Outside are sorcerers, the sexually immoral, murderers, idolaters and liars, in the lake of fire. faqs.question: What is a kingdom?
faqs.answer: An area ruled over by a king; the kingdom of God is a domain ruled over by God.

faqs.question: Do Christians still need incense and shadows?
faqs.answer: No—when we pray we are burning incense and lifting hands is the evening sacrifice; we have the real thing.

faqs.question: Is penance required for forgiveness?
faqs.answer: No penance or crawling or whipping—just come to Jesus, admit you’re wrong and ask him to forgive and cleanse you.

faqs.question: Is sin like a disease?
faqs.answer: He says the Bible refers to sin as a plague like leprosy, and Jesus heals and delivers us from it.

faqs.question: What counts as drunkenness?
faqs.answer: He says you don’t have to be staggering; intoxication is having enough alcohol to distort your judgment.

faqs.question: What is slander?
faqs.answer: Telling lies about someone or repeating a mistake they already turned from and corrected.

faqs.question: Can a Christian who stumbles be kicked out of the kingdom?
faqs.answer: He says you stay in when you admit wrong and grow; you’re out if you habitually keep sinning or say sin is okay.

faqs.question: Who killed Jesus?
faqs.answer: He says Jews and Romans carried it out, but anyone who chose to live wickedly pierced him—your sin crucified Jesus Christ.

faqs.question: How can you spot greedy ministers?
faqs.answer: He says they take two or three offerings in one service and promise you’ll get rich if you give to their ministry.

faqs.question: What is peace?
faqs.answer: The absence of conflict—when everyone treats each other right there is peace, and joy follows.
